newsitem.title: USA: Boston Fed economist says Fed eyeing inflation.
newsitem.headline: Boston Fed economist says Fed eyeing inflation.

text.p: The Federal Reserve monitors the overall trend of inflation, but is careful not to overemphasize any one piece of economic data, said an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston.

Boston Fed economist Jeffrey Fuhrer, speaking to reporters after the release of U.S. August payrolls data showing the unemployment rate dropping to 5.1 percent, said the Federal Reserve would continue to watch for changes in the inflation trend.
"The Fed is never going to overweight one number," Fuhrer said.
The payrolls data also revealed a five cent rise in average hourly earnings, while the headline number rose by 250,000.
"As a macroeconomist, I would say it's important to look at the trend, not what happened in August," Fuhrer said.
"Those month to month variations in the labor force don't mean that much to me."
He said there were no clear indications of an upturn in the inflation trend, although the Fed would maintain a sharp lookout.
"Are there clear signs that there are emerging demand pressures that would change the trend (inflation) rate? There's no conclusive evidence of that yet," Fuhrer said.
Fuhrer also said the level of tightness in the labor market was not just a measurement of the unemployment rate.

"Because of some other developments -- pretty good manufacturing activity and very favorable benefits cost developments -- if there were demand pressures, they did not manifest themselves in inflation."
Fuhrer said these developments may be temporary, but to the extent they continue, they would provide good news on inflation.
